issue_context.title: NUMA-aware scheduling (integration with Topology Manager)
issue_context.body:
This is a discussion thread followed from Topology Manager KEP's PR #1674:
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1674

**Description of a problem:** 
A scheduler is not NUMA aware and can schedule a pod to the node where the topology requirement of resources won't be satisfied and a pod will result in `Terminated` state.
comments:
> Yep, hence my second question: is really NFD a good place to expose this information? Reasons I'm asking:
> 1. AFAIU node-feature-labels aren't supposed to change very often; surely the node allocation changes very frequently, so I wonder if this is the right approach to convey this information. Maybe we should move in the direction of the prometheus node_exporter ?

Yes, you're right. NFD by default checks value per 60 seconds but this is configurable. 
Actually approach with NFD is rather not preferable (it is an example for a way to mitigate this problem but maybe not the best way to solve the problem in a long-term way) and we are focused now to prepare some possible approaches (for scheduling) and to discuss them with the community. 

> 2. did you planned already about how to extract the current allocation values (e.g. how many cores per-NUMA are actually being allocated) and expose them?

This is still to consider.

> 
> > 1. did you planned already about how to extract the current allocation values (e.g. how many cores per-NUMA are actually being allocated) and expose them?
> 
> This is still to consider.

Thanks, makes sense and really looking forward to hear your proposals. I've been researching and working in this area (together with @cynepco3hahue @vpickard @slintes and others), and we'd be happy to share what we tried and what we discarded, and why.

For example, I was researching a PoC to exfiltrate data from kubelet reading the checkpoint files, but we quickly (re)discovered this approach delivers poor data quality and it is thus unreliable.

Nice proposal!
If the newly introduced `topology policy` field will be embedded directly into `Pod.Spec`, should it be a generic policy but not only related with `NUMA` ?  The `single-nuwa-node` policy looks weird.

As for GPU resources, pods on the same node can be achieved with refined resource allocation through topology strategies, e.g: inter-pods communications by `nvlink` with topology policy `best-effort`, the topology manager hints a gpu allocation plan and allocate gpu cards in the same link.

Can we add a field on the node and pod api?
Node.status.topology field is managed by kubelet, show the topology collected by kubelet, for example:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Node
status:
  topology:
    # Group by NUMA. Looking forward to other topologies, such as nvlink.
    numaNode:
      # numa id
      "0":
        # core resource
        "cpu": 2
        # deivce plugin reported resource
        "nvidia.com/gpu": 1
```
and add a field on the pod resource, this field manage by kubelet, set on kubelet allocate resource for pod.
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
status:
  topology:
    numaNode:
      "0":
        "cpu": 2
        "nvidia.com/gpu": 1
```
then, we can easily write scheduling strategy based on topology.

review_comments:
I think we should not make dummy container spec or pod spec here.

The reason is, Topology Manager allocates resources while calculating topology hint.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/topologymanager/topology_manager.go#L232
The logic of `Admit` function is :
- for containers in Pod Spec(iteration)
  - getTopologyHints
  - merge Hints then determine admission
  - allocate //it allocate actual resources for pod

So if we using dummy Pod here, hint provider will allocate actual resources for dummy Pod.
And the allocated resources for dummy Pod will be released by garbage collector(reconciler) of each hint provider(CPU Manager and Device Manager).
(In reconciler it compares activePods with Pods that the hint provider allocates resources, if reconciler found stale pod, it frees the resource allocation of stale pod, see here for [reconciler](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f9532e46632f487363d8e1b499f92c854b905189/pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/cpu_manager.go#L306) for cpu manager, see [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f9532e46632f487363d8e1b499f92c854b905189/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/manager.go#L618) for reconciler for device manager)

So I would say `canAssignPod` would call `CheckPodAdditions` with Pod spec in http reuqest.

@bg-chun thanks, this answers my question above re: resource deallocation. However this seems to suggest that with the current code the only thing to do would be to start the pod in the first node that could accomodate the pod. There is no real option to try to fit a pod but not run it unless we do further refactoring in the topology manager, and I'm not sure how invasive that could be.

I excluded Allocate from RESTfull call path. Reservation would be done by following way: NodeInfo.RequestedResource from scheduler would be passed to kubelet each time we make a request. CPU/DeviceManager should take into account this value.
Does Reservation mean a excluding resources from v1.node object?

No, Reservation here means taking into account resources for the pod which was already assigned to the node (Bind), but not yet started. I saw your comment in https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1SR6XSIFsHkiWTws66LABpTiZaRwYk8IoRts4HQWE8Bc/edit#slide=id.g74d9a6aad0_0_109. I hurried, skipAllocate works only for pod level resources or when we have only one container in request.
